annotations.title: What a mod is, from its catalog page

description: What one Minecraft mod is and where to get it: its Modrinth page (title, summary, categories, loaders, the Minecraft releases its author lists, client/server side, licence, downloads, source and issue links) next to a short Modkeel lab record (tested versions, run and pair counts). Use it for "what does this mod do?", "is it client-only?", "where do I download it?" or to link a suspect from diagnose_crash. The versions here are what the author declares; for what the lab saw run or crash, use get_mod_runs, and for two mods together, check_mod_pair. Takes a lab mod id or a Modrinth slug; from a name, call search_mods first. The project is matched by the SHA-1 of a jar the lab ran (source: jar_hash, exact), else by slug (source: slug); a mod on neither returns found: false, not an error. Asks Modrinth live on each call (nothing cached here), so it can fail when Modrinth is down: retry later.

mod_id.description: Lab mod id (e.g. fabric_api, ferritecore) or Modrinth slug (e.g. fabric-api, sodium-extra), lowercase. Unsure? Call search_mods first.
